name: multilingual-classics-markdown
description: A curated corpus of public-domain literary classics in 53 languages across 66 locales, converted to clean Markdown with YAML frontmatter. It spans 14 language families and 19 script systems, including Latin with rich diacritics, Cyrillic, polytonic Greek, Hebrew, Arabic, Perso-Arabic, Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati, Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Tibetan, Han, kana, Hangul, the Thai abugida, the Cherokee syllabary, three constructed auxiliary languages, and the historical stages of English from Old English to original-spelling Early Modern. Every text is public domain in the United States and carries per-record provenance: the upstream archive, the exact source URL fetched, the publication year of the cited source edition, and notes recording what was excerpted, corrected or left alone. Books whose text falls below the corpus fidelity bar declare a machine-readable text_quality tier so they can be filtered out in one line. Built as a drop-in multilingual test corpus for rendering and typography work, and usable as a small, clean, permissively licensed literary dataset.
dataCollection: Texts were sourced from volunteer digitisation projects (Project Gutenberg, per-language Wikisource, Aozora Bunko, Project Ben-Yehuda, Ganjoor, the Saga Database, Project Madurai, NZETC and the Internet Archive) and converted with per-source scripts held in scripts/. Selection is curated rather than exhaustive: canonical works are preferred, sacred and liturgical texts are excluded by default, with a narrow, flagged exception for recovered texts and for scripts with no other witness, and each locale carries two or three works where sources permitted. Every substitution and judgment call is recorded in CORPUS.md.
dataBiases: This is a convenience corpus, not a collection of critical editions, and it inherits the transcription errors of the projects it draws on. No text has been collated against manuscripts. Coverage is uneven by design and by the state of digitisation: European languages are better served than African and Asian ones, and where a language's pre-1929 digitised corpus is overwhelmingly missionary-religious, the corpus falls back on reference works, which is documented per locale. Several works of collected oral literature passed through colonial-era editors whose names displaced those of the source authors and informants; where scholarship identifies those authors the frontmatter credits them. Curation reflects one maintainer's judgment about what counts as canon.

distribution.name: repository
distribution.description: The corpus git repository. Clone it, or pin a wave-YYYY-MM-DD tag for a reviewed snapshot.

distribution.name: manifest.json
distribution.description: Machine-readable index of every book: path, locale, full frontmatter, size and word count. Validated in CI against manifest.schema.json.

distribution.name: books
distribution.description: One Markdown file per work, at books/<bcp47-locale>/<author>/<title>.md, each opening with a YAML frontmatter block.

recordSet.name: books_index
recordSet.description: One record per work, drawn from manifest.json. The 145 records cover 66 locales. Fields mirror the YAML frontmatter specified in FRONTMATTER.md.

field.name: path
field.description: Repo-relative path to the Markdown file. This is the identity of a book; renames land in dedicated commits so they can be tracked with git diff --find-renames.

field.name: locale
field.description: BCP-47 tag carrying region and script subtags where they matter, for example es-MX, zh-Hans, pt-BR.

field.name: title
field.description: The work's title in its own language and orthography.

field.name: author
field.description: The author in their own language where the source gives it. May carry combined attribution for collected oral literature.

field.name: year
field.description: Publication year of the cited source edition, as a string. Approximate and era-qualified forms occur, for example c. 1280 and c. 399 BCE.

field.name: yearNumeric
field.description: The year reduced to a sortable integer, negative for BCE. Ranges from -500 to 1925.

field.name: source
field.description: The upstream archive the text came from.

field.name: license
field.description: Constant across the corpus: Public domain in the United States. Where the public-domain basis is anything other than straightforward pre-1929 publication, the basis is stated in source_note.

field.name: text_quality
field.description: Present only on books known to fall short of the corpus fidelity bar, so consumers can filter them out. noisy means unproofread OCR with disclosed residual noise; alpha means known substantial problems, provisional. Absent by default. Every tagged book has a matching open flag in QUALITY.md.

field.name: sacred_text
field.description: Present only on a sacred, liturgical or cult text admitted under the narrow exception in README curation principle 2, naming its route: recovered-text (the work was lost and is known only from excavation, rediscovery or decipherment) or sole-witness (the one standard text in a script the corpus cannot otherwise carry). Absent by default, meaning admitted under the normal secular rule.

field.name: wordCount
field.description: Whitespace-delimited word count of the body. Not meaningful for the scriptio continua languages (ja, zh, th), where it approximates line or character runs instead.

field.name: sizeBytes
field.description: Size of the Markdown file on disk, frontmatter included.

recordSet.name: book_files
recordSet.description: One record per Markdown file. Join to books_index on filepath, which equals the manifest's path field.

field.name: filepath
field.description: Path of the Markdown file within the repository. Equal to the path field of books_index; join on this.

field.name: content
field.description: The Markdown file itself: the YAML frontmatter block followed by the body text.
